thread:
kevin_dev: Heads-up — trying the new JS SDK in Cloudflare Workers and auth path blows up. Error: "ReferenceError: process is not defined". SDK currently calls process.env for SERVICE_TOKEN fallback.

maya_sdk: yep that's expected. Workers don't have Node globals. We should not rely on process.env there — use binding/env passed to the worker.

kevin_dev: I worked around it with: 
```js
const token = typeof process !== 'undefined' && process.env.SERVICE_TOKEN
  ? process.env.SERVICE_TOKEN
  : (globalThis.__REDWOOD_SERVICE_TOKEN__ || null);
```
But feels hacky. Also noticed streaming + AbortController behaves slightly different (no node stream).

maya_sdk: Agreed hacky. We should implement a small platform adapter layer in the SDK: { fetch: globalThis.fetch, crypto: globalThis.crypto, envLookup: () => globalThis.__REDWOOD_BINDINGS__ } and let the worker import an adapter that reads from env vars via bindings provided at deploy-time.

sasha_pm: Prioritize? This is blocking an internal POC. Customers will hit it too. Can we ship a quick patch to avoid referencing process at module top-level?

maya_sdk: Yes — quick plan: 1) remove any top-level process.env references, 2) add runtime-safe env getter: getEnv('SERVICE_TOKEN') that tries (in order): globalThis.__REDWOOD_BINDINGS__, globalThis.__REDWOOD_SERVICE_TOKEN__, process?.env, and finally undefined. 3) export a small helper file workers-adapter.ts with types for ESM/CJS compatibility.

kevin_dev: Also watch bundlers — esbuild/rollup sometimes polyfill process for dev, then code works locally but breaks in prod. We should document that explicitly in the worker guide.

maya_sdk: Good call. We should also provide an example worker quickstart. Something like:
```js
// worker.js
import { RedwoodClient } from 'redwood-sdk/worker-adapter'
export default {
  async fetch(request, env) {
    const client = new RedwoodClient({
      fetch: globalThis.fetch,
      crypto: globalThis.crypto,
      getSecret: (name) => env[name]
    })
    const res = await client.generate({ prompt: 'hi' })
    return new Response(res.text)
  }
}
```

sasha_pm: Nice. Add note about WebCrypto vs Node crypto (crypto.subtle is available but API differs). We should polyfill digest helpers in the adapter.

infra-bot: CI: build-redwood-sdk #642 failed on linux (esm/cjs interop test) — logs: "Cannot find module 'worker-adapter'"

maya_sdk: infra-bot — that CI failure is related: we had conditional exports in package.json that weren't picking up in the test runner. Fix is to ensure the worker-adapter file is present in both cjs and esm build outputs (or ship it as pure ESM and document how to import in CJS).

kevin_dev: One more gotcha: fetch timeout/retry logic. Workers don't support AbortSignal.timeout in older runtimes. Our retry helper should not assume AbortController.timeout exists. Use manual setTimeout->abort approach. Also make retry backoff configurable.

maya_sdk: I'll open a PR with: - platform adapter + worker quickstart - runtime-safe env getter - crypto digest helper - improved retry that uses setTimeout fallback - docs note about bundlers and conditional exports.

sasha_pm: Awesome. Can you add a short blurb to onboarding checklist so solutions engineers know to bind secrets instead of expecting process.env?

kevin_dev: Will test PR once it's up. Thanks :thumbsup:

maya_sdk: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/891 — includes examples and timeline.

kevin_dev: Verified the PR fixes my case locally. Streaming still needs a tiny tweak for ReadableStream BYOB differences but not blocking.

sasha_pm: Great progress. Let's track follow-ups in the SDK board.
